articles.snippet:
Pivot Energy closed a $173 million term loan facility supporting a portfolio of 51 community-scale solar projects totaling 135 MWdc across six states. First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank, and BankUnited provided the takeout financing.
The post Pivot Energy Closes $173 Million Term Loan With First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank And BankUnited appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Pivot Energy Closes $173 Million Term Loan With First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank And BankUnited
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Pivot Energy Closes $173 Million Term Loan With First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank And BankUnited
Pivot Energy closed a $173 million term loan facility supporting a portfolio of 51 community-scale solar projects totaling 135 MWdc across six states. First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank, and BankUnited provided the takeout financing.
The transaction represents Pivot Energy’s first term loan financing.
The facility refinances projects previously funded through Pivot’s construction warehouse and consolidates its first three portfolios under a single term structure.
Pivot said the financing also frees capacity within its revolving construction facility, allowing the company to continue building additional renewable energy projects.
The 51-project portfolio includes distributed-scale solar developments serving communities and customers across six states.
Pivot develops, owns, and operates solar and energy storage projects across the U.S.
The company said the new capital structure gives it additional flexibility to expand while continuing investments in community benefits, agrivoltaics, local employment, and economic development.
Pivot Energy is an ECP portfolio company.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing our first term loan across a consolidated portfolio is an important step for Pivot. We’re grateful to First Citizens, Huntington, and BankUnited, who have supported Pivot from the start. This financing gives us the flexibility to grow faster and deliver lasting value where our projects are built.”
Bret Labadie, Chief Financial Officer of Pivot Energy
“This financing reflects the strength and diversity of Pivot’s distributed solar portfolio, and we’re proud to support the company through its next stage of growth.”
Mike Lorusso, Head of Energy Finance at First Citizens Bank

articles.title: CrownPoint Partners Tops $160 Million In 2026 Closed Deal Volume
articles.snippet:
CrownPoint Partners surpassed $160 million in year-to-date transaction volume during 2026 and entered the fourth quarter with more than $275 million of deals under agreement or actively listed.
The post CrownPoint Partners Tops $160 Million In 2026 Closed Deal Volume appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
CrownPoint Partners Tops $160 Million In 2026 Closed Deal Volume
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
CrownPoint Partners Tops $160 Million In 2026 Closed Deal Volume
CrownPoint Partners surpassed $160 million in year-to-date transaction volume during 2026 and entered the fourth quarter with more than $275 million of deals under agreement or actively listed.
Combined, the firm’s closed transactions and current pipeline exceed $435 million.
CrownPoint’s 2026 activity spans healthcare properties, dental real estate, quick-service restaurants, automotive properties, car washes, and value-add investment opportunities.
The real estate brokerage represents business owners, institutional investors, developers, and private investors on both acquisitions and sales.
Healthcare and dental sale-leasebacks and investment sales have been particularly active areas for the firm during 2026.
CrownPoint has also completed net lease retail transactions involving nationally recognized brands.
The firm’s business includes both marketed properties and off-market transactions.
CrownPoint expects transaction activity to continue through the remainder of 2026 as it advances its existing pipeline and expands relationships across its investment sales and sale-leaseback businesses.
KEY QUOTES:
“As we surpass $160 million in closed volume, what stands out most is the momentum we are carrying into the fourth quarter.”
Julius Swolsky, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of CrownPoint Partners
“A significant portion of our business comes from repeat clients who trust us to execute across different markets, asset types and investment strategies.”
Shannon Bona, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of CrownPoint Partners
“We have a substantial pipeline in place, and our priority is continuing to deliver results for our clients while strategically growing the CrownPoint platform.”
Don Bingham III, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of CrownPoint Partners

articles.title: Generate Capital And KeyState Close $154.5 Million Community Solar Tax Equity Fund
articles.snippet:
Generate Capital closed a $154.5 million tax equity commitment with SOLCAP, KeyState's tax equity investment platform, supporting 10 community solar projects across New York and Illinois. The portfolio totals 43 MWac of generation capacity.
The post Generate Capital And KeyState Close $154.5 Million Community Solar Tax Equity Fund appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Generate Capital And KeyState Close $154.5 Million Community Solar Tax Equity Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Generate Capital And KeyState Close $154.5 Million Community Solar Tax Equity Fund
Generate Capital closed a $154.5 million tax equity commitment with SOLCAP, KeyState’s tax equity investment platform, supporting 10 community solar projects across New York and Illinois. The portfolio totals 43 MWac of generation capacity.
The transaction represents the sixth tax equity fund between Generate and KeyState.
Their partnership began in 2021 and has focused on channeling institutional capital into distributed clean energy infrastructure.
The new fund follows an $85 million community solar tax equity fund announced by Generate and KeyState in October 2025.
That earlier vehicle is now nearing final funding.
Generate said the latest transaction also builds on broader capital-raising momentum across its infrastructure platform.
The company has secured approximately $1.6 billion in financing commitments so far in 2026 to support deployment of critical infrastructure.
Generate entered the community solar market in 2017 and has since built a large distributed solar investment and operating platform.
The company works with capital providers, developers, utilities, and other partners to finance and deploy community-scale clean energy projects.
Generate said the new fund will help expand access to reliable and cost-effective clean power for customers and communities.
For KeyState, the transaction continues the expansion of its SOLCAP platform, which is designed to connect institutional capital with tax equity investment opportunities.
The partners said the structure allows them to support community solar projects at greater scale while providing investment opportunities tied to distributed power infrastructure.
Willis Towers Watson served as the investment tax credit insurance broker for the transaction.
Holland & Knight represented Generate as legal counsel.
Generate was founded in 2014 and develops, finances, builds, owns, and operates infrastructure across energy and other essential services.
Since its founding, the company has raised more than $10 billion in capital.
KEY QUOTES:
“Long-term capital partnerships are essential to our ability to scale critical infrastructure and meet growing demand for power.”
Peggy Flannery, Managing Director and Head of Distributed Generation at Generate Capital
“Our sixth fund with KeyState reflects both the strength of our longstanding partnership and continued interest from institutional capital providers in investing alongside Generate. Together, we’re putting capital to work in projects that expand access to reliable, cost-effective clean power for communities across the country.”
Peggy Flannery, Managing Director and Head of Distributed Generation at Generate Capital
“Generate has been a trusted partner to KeyState and the SOLCAP platform for more than five years, and this sixth fund reflects the strength and consistency of that relationship.”
Allan Riska, Chief Investment Officer at KeyState
“Together, we’ve been able to bring institutional capital to high-quality community solar projects at meaningful scale. We’re pleased to deepen our partnership with Generate and continue investing in projects that deliver both compelling investment opportunities and tangible benefits for communities and ratepayers.”
Allan Riska, Chief Investment Officer at KeyState

E&S Insurtech Ledgebrook Raises $65 Million
June 25, 2025
Email This
Subscribe to Newsletter
Article
Ledgebrook Inc, a technology-driven excess and surplus lines managing general agency, recently completed the close of a $65 million funding round.
The oversubscribed Series C round was led by existing investor The Stephens Group, LLC . Existing investors Duquesne, Brand Foundry, Floating Point, and American Family Ventures participated in the round, alongside new investors including Hummingbird Nomads.
Gage Caligaris, founder and chief executive officer of the Massachusetts-based Ledgebrook, said the funding will allow the MGA to bring in additional talent to grow and enhance its service to wholesale brokers, offer new insurance products through its platform, and participate further in retaining risk on the insurance it is writing on behalf of its carrier partners.
The firm offers general and professional liability products.
Ledgebrook management and employees will continue to be the largest shareholders in the company. Ryan Morrow, managing director at Stephens Group, will join Ledgebrook’s board of directors.
“The round recognizes the momentum in our business. It positions Ledgebrook to truly establish itself as a premier E&S platform, known for consistent execution on our mission to delight wholesale brokers and for bringing together the best of insurance expertise and technology,” Caligaris said.
Ledgebrook was founded in March 2002, when it raised $4.2 million in seed funding. Since the it has raised another $4.6 million, $24 million and $17 million.
Prior to entering insurance, Ledgebrook founder Caligaris traded commodity derivatives at Barclays. His insurance career started in the actuarial program at Liberty Mutual, where he rose to become senior director of new mobility products.
John Mullen serves as president of E&S for Ledgebrook. Mullen has experience as a retail broker and an E&S underwriter and has worked for multiple regional and global insurance carriers. He joined Ledgebrook from Liberty Mutual.
The Stephens Group is a private investment firm with more than $2 billion of private equity assets under management. Since 2006, Stephens Group has invested in more than 50 companies, targeting industries including industrial products and services, specialty distribution, and vertical software.

articles.title: VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility From Viola Credit To Expand Payroll-Linked Consumer Lending
articles.snippet:
VIVA Finance, an Atlanta-based financial technology company specializing in payroll-linked consumer lending, has secured a $150 million credit facility from Viola Credit to expand its lending operations and increase access to affordable personal loans.
The post VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility From Viola Credit To Expand Payroll-Linked Consumer Lending appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility From Viola Credit To Expand Payroll-Linked Consumer Lending
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility From Viola Credit To Expand Payroll-Linked Consumer Lending
VIVA Finance, an Atlanta-based financial technology company specializing in payroll-linked consumer lending, has secured a $150 million credit facility from Viola Credit to expand its lending operations and increase access to affordable personal loans.
The financing will provide VIVA Finance with additional lending capacity as it scales its proprietary payroll-linked credit platform and expands its reach among consumers who have limited access to traditional financial products.
Founded by CEO Jack Markwalter, VIVA Finance focuses on helping working Americans access personal loans through a model that integrates repayments directly with employees’ direct deposits.
Rather than relying exclusively on conventional credit evaluation and repayment mechanisms, the company uses its payroll-linked infrastructure to support responsible underwriting and more predictable loan repayments.
This structure is designed to reduce lending risk and enable VIVA to offer competitive loan terms and lower interest rates than many traditional personal loan alternatives.
The company’s approach targets a segment of the consumer finance market that frequently faces challenges obtaining affordable credit through traditional banks and credit bureaus.
These consumers may encounter limited financing options during unexpected expenses or financial emergencies, potentially pushing them toward higher-cost borrowing alternatives.
VIVA aims to address this gap by offering transparent personal loans with repayment arrangements integrated into existing payroll processes.
The new $150 million facility represents a significant expansion of VIVA’s financing resources and is expected to support growth in loan originations, customer acquisition, and distribution partnerships.
The transaction also builds on the company’s recent efforts to expand its presence across the employee benefits and consumer credit ecosystem.
VIVA has developed strategic distribution relationships intended to make its lending products available through platforms already serving working Americans.
One such relationship is its partnership with BenefitHub, which selected VIVA as a preferred personal loan provider for its Benefits+ voluntary benefits platform. The arrangement integrates VIVA’s lending products into employee benefits offerings, potentially broadening its reach among workers seeking financial wellness solutions.
Viola Credit, the lender supporting the new facility, is a global credit asset manager with approximately $5 billion in assets under management.
The firm specializes in asset-based lending and growth capital for technology-enabled financial services companies, including businesses operating across fintech, property technology, and insurance technology.
Viola Credit has completed more than $3.5 billion in asset-based lending transactions across the United States, United Kingdom, Western Europe, and Australia.
Its investment strategy focuses on providing financing to companies developing technologies and business models that challenge traditional financial markets.
For VIVA Finance, the partnership provides access to institutional credit capital and structured finance expertise as it expands its consumer lending business.

articles.title: EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland
articles.snippet:
EZO has reached financial close on a €150 million investment-grade, non-recourse senior debt facility to finance the development of more than 3,000 electric vehicle charge points across the UK and Ireland.
The post EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
EZO Secures €150 Million Senior Debt Facility To Accelerate EV Charging Expansion Across The UK And Ireland
EZO has reached financial close on a €150 million investment-grade, non-recourse senior debt facility to finance the development of more than 3,000 electric vehicle charge points across the UK and Ireland.
The financing will support the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of charging infrastructure representing more than 100,000 kW of capacity. Most of the planned sites will be developed under long-term public-sector concession arrangements with features similar to public-private partnerships.
EZO estimates the charge points could generate well over £1 billion in electricity sales during the next 20 years. A portion of that revenue will be shared with public-sector partners, and the chargers are expected to revert to the public sector when the applicable concessions end.
The debt financing was provided by a consortium of lenders including Aberdeen Investments and Standard Life. EZO said the structure is believed to represent the first investment-grade financing of its type for EV chargers across the UK and Ireland, with revenue generated by the assets ring-fenced to repay the debt over a seven-year period.
Ireland-headquartered EZO has been expanding rapidly into mainland Britain and expects the UK to become its primary EV charging market by 2027. The company has secured local authority-backed public charging contracts in the UK with a combined estimated value exceeding £1 billion.
These agreements include a 20-year concession spanning four counties in Northern Scotland and a 15-year concession across four counties in the English Midlands. EZO said it expects to announce additional significant public-sector contracts in the coming months as it pursues opportunities across Scotland, England, and Wales.
The concessions can include access to desirable charging locations, flexible pricing, regional exclusivity, help with permits and grid connections, and, in some cases, public funding to support deployment. Certain arrangements also include revenue-sharing mechanisms designed to return value to the public sector over time.
EZO is majority owned by Rubicon Capital Management and affiliated entities, including Rubicon Capital Advisors. Rubicon initially acquired a 35% interest in EZO in 2020 and has since increased its ownership to more than 60%, including additional shares acquired alongside the latest financing.
The shareholder group has also added Whitehole, a Spain-based family office with experience in electrification technologies supporting sustainable mobility. Rubicon acted as sole financial advisor to EZO on both the debt and equity capital raises and has been retained to explore additional financing options, including a potential IPO in 2028.

articles.title: Rocket Pharmaceuticals Secures Up To $150 Million Credit Facility From Hercules Capital
articles.snippet:
Rocket Pharmaceuticals has secured a credit facility of up to $150 million from Hercules Capital to strengthen its financial position and support the development of its cardiovascular genetic medicine pipeline.
The post Rocket Pharmaceuticals Secures Up To $150 Million Credit Facility From Hercules Capital appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Rocket Pharmaceuticals Secures Up To $150 Million Credit Facility From Hercules Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Rocket Pharmaceuticals Secures Up To $150 Million Credit Facility From Hercules Capital
Rocket Pharmaceuticals has secured a credit facility of up to $150 million from Hercules Capital to strengthen its financial position and support the development of its cardiovascular genetic medicine pipeline.
Rocket received $35 million at closing and can draw another $35 million during specified periods at its option, subject to the terms of the agreement.
An additional $30 million could become available following achievement of a specified clinical milestone related to Rocket’s Danon disease program.
A final $50 million tranche is subject to approval by Hercules Capital’s investment committee.
The facility includes an initial 30-month interest-only period and a 48-month maturity, with potential extensions if specified milestones are achieved. Hercules also received warrants to purchase Rocket common stock.
Rocket plans to use the financing to support its pivotal Phase 2 study of RP-A501 for Danon disease and advance its broader cardiovascular pipeline.
As of June 30, 2026, Rocket had $283.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments.
Based on its current operating plan, the company expects those resources plus the initial $35 million borrowing to finance operations into the third quarter of 2028.
If Rocket accesses additional amounts available through the Hercules facility, the company said its cash runway could extend into 2029, depending on borrowing conditions, future draws and operating expenditures.
The financing follows Rocket’s sale of a priority review voucher and is intended to diversify its sources of capital as it advances cardiovascular genetic medicine programs.
LifeSci Capital served as Rocket’s financial advisor on the term loan financing, and PJT served as a capital markets advisor.
KEY QUOTES:
“Building on the sale of our priority review voucher, this financing diversifies our sources of capital and strengthens our ability to execute and deliver on our cardiovascular strategy. The staged structure provides flexibility to align additional funding with progress across our programs. We remain focused on allocating capital thoughtfully, executing the pivotal Danon study and advancing genetic medicines for patients with serious inherited heart diseases.”
Gaurav Shah, M.D., CEO of Rocket Pharmaceuticals
“Rocket is advancing toward important milestones across its cardiovascular pipeline, led by the pivotal Danon program. We are pleased to provide a flexible financing solution that supports the Company’s development priorities. We look forward to working alongside Rocket as it builds on its expertise in cardiovascular genetic medicines.”
R. Bryan Jadot, Senior Managing Director and Group Head of Life Sciences at Hercules Capital
